text: Looking into it: gin.Error only implements Unwrap on the pointer receiver, so a value Error wrapped with fmt.Errorf can't be unwrapped. Fix in progress.
Confirmed: responseWriter.WriteHeader updates w.status even after the header was already written. Fix in progress.
Confirmed: the Context pool allocates the params slice from maxParams at pool-creation time, so routes added later get an undersized slice. Fix in progress.
Fixed: gin.Error.Unwrap now has a value receiver, so a value gin.Error wrapped with fmt.Errorf unwraps correctly (errors.Is/errors.As true); the pointer form still works. Running final verification.

Fixed: responseWriter.WriteHeader now returns early (keeping the debug warning) when the header was already written, so Status() keeps reporting the status that was actually sent. Running final verification.

Fixed: handleHTTPRequest now grows the pooled context's params/skippedNodes slices when routes registered later raised maxParams/maxSections, so params are populated for late-registered routes. Running final verification.

Done and verified: errors.go — `func (msg Error) Unwrap() error` (value receiver). Value-form gin.Error now unwraps, so errors.Is/errors.As succeed; pointer form unchanged. Full test suite still green.

Done and verified: response_writer.go — WriteHeader returns early (keeping the [WARNING] debug message) once the header has been written, so Status() reports the status actually sent (200, not 401). Full test suite still green.

Done and verified: gin.go — handleHTTPRequest now reallocates the pooled context's params/skippedNodes when routes registered after the first request raised maxParams/maxSections. Late-registered /test/:name/:last_name/*wild now yields name=john, last_name=smith, wild=/is/super/great (and no more slice-bounds panic). Full test suite still green.
Confirmed: findCaseInsensitivePathRec navigates to children[0] while the wildcard child is stored last, so it walks into the wrong node type and panics. Fix in progress.
Confirmed: the NegotiateFormat matching loop indexes offer[i] without a length check, so a longer Accept entry panics. Fix in progress.
Confirmed: FileAttachment writes the ASCII filename into Content-Disposition without escaping quotes/backslashes. Fix in progress.

Fixed: NegotiateFormat's compare loop now stops at the shorter string (no out-of-range panic); an accepted format that is a prefix of the offer still matches as before. Suite green apart from a leftover scratch test file that I am removing now.
